text:
sylvia: Heads-up — canary rollout to ap-southeast-1 is stuck. traffic-split shows 0% shifted even though controller reported 5% success. Pods are Pending with GPU scheduling failures.

infra-bot: alert: nodepool-provisioner failed to create nodepool 'gpu-pool-ap-southeast-1-a' (quota/error). Terraform drift detected on subnet tags. See: https://console.ops/reports/TFDRIFT/1765554321 :warning: 

dan: logs? events? suspect autoscaler can't attach instances due to subnet tag mismatch (we hit this pattern before).

lee: kubectl describe on one pending pod shows: 
```
Events:
  Normal  Scheduled  3m  default-scheduler  Successfully assigned ... but then
  Warning FailedScheduling  2m  pod-binding  0/4 nodes are available: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```
Seems nodes didn't spin up.

maria: Can we pause the progressive delivery? We should stop the ramp while infra surfaces. I can flip traffic-split to keep prod at baseline. :hand:

sylvia: yes please pause. lee — can you run the pause? deploy-bot should also halt automated ramps.

deploy-bot: auto-rollout: detected canary job 2026-03-18-1765554321. current traffic 5%. pausing ramp per request. will not increase above 5% until manual resume.

dan: quick root cause summary: recent TF provider bump changed how we populate `k8s-subnet:managed=true` tag; autoscaler bootstrap IAM role uses that tag to attach new nodes to subnet. drift meant nodepool creation API returned 403, so no GPU nodes.

maria: short mitigation options: 1) restore previous terraform state for tag values (fast) 2) temporarily scale another GPU pool in eu region and re-route canary 3) fallback to cpu-quantized model variant for canary (lower perf but keeps tests running).

lee: I tried a manual reapply of the tag via terraform import + apply and it errored on provider version mismatch. rolling back provider to v4 in staging would be quick but prod is sensitive.

sylvia: decision: pause traffic (done), restore the subnet tag via cloud console (SRE), then verify nodepool create, then resume. fallback to CPU model is standby if we can't get GPUs within 30m.

infra-bot: runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/gpu-provisioning. assigned: infra-sre (dan) + infra-oncall (lee). expected ETA 25-40m.

dan: I'll own the console fix and a minimal TF rollback if console patch doesn't stick. lee — can you watch autoscaler logs and post `kubectl get events -w` output?

lee: watching now. if we see `InstanceCreationRateLimitExceeded` or `AccessDenied` I'll escalate to cloud infra.

maria: if we need to flip model variant, I can push a canary override to the model-router: `model-router set canary-variant=cpu-quant-v2` and keep traffic 5% to validate correctness.

sylvia: thanks all — thumbs-up to the plan. will update once nodepool is healthy or we trigger fallback. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: update: canary ramp remains paused. audit note logged.

lee: quick note — add a small helm postStart delay for the gpu-prober hook in canary chart to avoid helm hook races during node churn (followup ticket created: #INFRA-5123).
